label: Alcohol and Drinking
framing: Scripture blesses wine as a gift that gladdens the heart and warns in the same breath against the cup that masters a person. The line is not between drink and no drink but between the one who holds the cup and the one the cup has begun to hold.
cultural: Wine was woven through ordinary life in the ancient world, drunk at meals and weddings, used as medicine, and poured out in worship, and Jesus himself made it at Cana and shared it at the last supper. Yet the same Scriptures that honor wine paint drunkenness without mercy, from Noah uncovered in his tent to the long warning of the wise father, because a culture that loved its wine knew exactly what it cost when it ruled a man.
historical: Augustine, in the late fourth century, told in his Confessions how his mother Monica, as a girl, slipped into a habit of secret drinking until a servant's taunt shamed her out of it, a story he had from her own lips, and he wrote of his own daily struggle to rule appetite in eating and drinking. The church has held the freedom of the gift and the warning of the snare together for two thousand years, and in the modern age has stood alongside the recovery movements that have walked countless people, one day at a time, out of the bottle and back into their lives.
application: Be honest about whether you still hold the cup or it now holds you, and trust the people who love you if they say what you cannot yet admit. If you have tried to stop and could not, that is not weakness but addiction, and addiction is healed in the open, with help, not in shame and alone. Reach out to a wise friend, a pastor, a doctor, and in the United States to free, confidential help any hour at SAMHSA, 1-800-662-4357.

verses.text: Do not get drunk on wine, which leads to reckless indiscretion. Instead, be filled with the Spirit.
Wine is a mocker, strong drink is a brawler, and whoever is led astray by them is not wise.
Do not gaze at wine while it is red, when it sparkles in the cup and goes down smoothly. In the end it bites like a snake and stings like a viper.

He makes the grass grow for the livestock and provides crops for man to cultivate, bringing forth food from the earth: wine that gladdens the heart of man, oil that makes his face to shine, and bread that sustains his heart.
“Everything is permissible for me,” but not everything is beneficial. “Everything is permissible for me,” but I will not be mastered by anything.
